name: AKU Chair of Paediatrics named GoalKeeper2030

content.title: AKU Chair of Paediatrics named GoalKeeper2030
content.summary: Dr Fyezah Jehan, Chair of Paediatrics represented Pakistan at the Gates Foundation annual event

media.alt: AKU Chair of Paediatrics named GoalKeeper2030

content.text: The Chair of Paediatrics & Child Health, Associate Professor Dr Fyezah Jehan, represented Pakistan at the prestigious Gates Foundation annual Goalkeepers 2030 event in New York on September 20 for her efforts to enhance the survival of premature babies. She was selected as one of the global 'Goalkeepers' by the Gates Foundation.

Goalkeepers are individuals who have been working on sustainable development goals. The 17 SDGs set by world leaders in 2015 and agreed upon by all member states of the United Nations including Pakistan, are to be attained by 2030.

Dr Jehan spoke about the groundbreaking research being done at the Department of Paediatrics & Child Health at AKU on studying how gut bacteria plays a part in the survival of premature babies. "There is much more to learn about the microbiome but what we do know now can greatly increase the survival odds of a baby allowing it to develop and grow well beyond the first 30 days of life," explained Dr Jehan. She also shared how certain equipment can be used to help them breathe better when their lungs are struggling.

Such innovations are the focus of this year's GoalKeepers 2030 report. For example, it talks about saving mothers' lives by preventing blood loss after giving birth (post-partum hemorrhage) commonly caused by anemia, or a severe iron deficiency. AKU's Department of Paediatrics & Child Health has already been giving IV iron to quickly replenish pregnant women's iron reserves at its peri-urban study sites in Karachi during routine antenatal care it offers the community. These women are also given the antibiotic azithromycin when they go into labour to boost their ability to fight infection, reducing their chances of developing deadly sepsis, an intervention also mentioned by the Gates Foundation as one that reduces maternal mortality rates.

"As I embarked on my journey to attend this event, I couldn't help but recognize the millions of journeys our mothers and infants undertake every day, the miracle of pregnancy, the joy of giving birth, the immense strength that a baby shows when recovering from an infectious disease," said Dr Jehan. "We are reminded of the courage and endurance of our people and of humanity. That is why I am optimistic and I imagine a world where the future is brighter and kinder for everyone."
